decision.explanation: Multiply rows of A by columns of B, using i² = −1. The entries are (1−2i)−(5−i)=−4−i, (1+2i)+(5−i)(2i)=3+12i, i(1−2i)+3i=2+4i, and i(1+2i)+(−3i)(2i)=4+i. Thus option d is correct.

after.worked_solution:
Multiplying the matrices using the usual method, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 5-\text{i} \\ \text{i} & -3\text{i}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1-2\text{i} & 1+2\text{i} \\ -1 & 2\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(1)(1-2\text{i})+(5-\text{i})(-1) & (1)(1+2\text{i})+(5-\text{i})(2\text{i}) \\ (\text{i})(1-2\text{i})+(-3\text{i})(-1) & (\text{i})(1+2\text{i})+(-3\text{i})(2\text{i})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(1-2\text{i})+(-5+\text{i}) & (1+2\text{i})+(2+10\text{i}) \\ (2+\text{i})+(3\text{i}) & (-2+\text{i})+(6)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4-\text{i} & 3+12\text{i} \\ 2+4\text{i} & 4+\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
For the given matrix $A,$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2-\text{i} & 1+3\text{i} \\ -1-4\text{i} & 2-2\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(A)}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ -4 & -2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(A)}.\end{aligned}
$$

So we have $a=2,b=1,e=-1$ and $f=3.$ Therefore,

$$

content.problem: Find the imaginary part of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}8+\text{i} & 3-4\text{i} \\ 9 & \text{i}\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
For the given matrix $A,$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}8+\text{i} & 3-4\text{i} \\ 9 & \text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}8+\text{i} & 3-4\text{i} \\ 9+0\text{i} & 0+\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}8 & 3 \\ 9 & 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(A)}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(A)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\text{Im}(A)=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].$

decision.explanation: First divide row 1 by 2i to obtain [1, 3]. Then add (1−3i) times this updated row to row 2: −1+3i+(1−3i)=0 and −2+3(1−3i)=1−9i. The result matches option c.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
Given the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}2\text{i} & 6\text{i} \\ -1+3\text{i} & -2\end{aligned}]$, find the result of applying to $A$ the following elementary row operations: 

$$
{R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{2\text{i}}{R}_{1},\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(1-3\text{i}){R}_{1}
$$
after.worked_solution:
Let's apply the row operations to $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2\text{i} & 6\text{i} \\ -1+3\text{i} & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2\text{i}}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ -1+3\text{i} & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(1-3\text{i}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1-9\text{i}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the result  is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1-9\text{i}\end{aligned}].
$$

content.problem:
Given the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}2\text{i} & 6\text{i} \\ -1+3\text{i} & -2\end{aligned}]$, find the result of applying to $A$ the following elementary row operations: 

$$
{R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{2\text{i}}{R}_{1},\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(1-3\text{i}){R}_{1}
$$
content.worked_solution:
Let's apply the row operations to $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2\text{i} & 6\text{i} \\ -1+3\text{i} & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2\text{i}}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ -1+3\text{i} & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(1-3\text{i}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1-9\text{i}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the result  is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1-9\text{i}\end{aligned}].
$$
